judgments.reason: The span 'swelling of her right upper eyelid' appears literally in the vignette and clinically supports orbital/periorbital involvement as a complication of frontal sinusitis.

The span 'immovable scarlike node, 11 × 7 mm, on her right upper eyelid discharging pus' appears literally in the vignette and directly supports orbital/periorbital involvement with a draining lesion consistent with the modifier.

The span 'High signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus' appears literally in the vignette; however, this finding describes sinus pathology rather than orbital involvement. It supports chronic frontal sinusitis but does not directly support the 'orbital involvement' component of the modifier. Nevertheless, it is part of the imaging context for the completed diagnosis.

The span 'Opacification on right frontal sinus, right ethmoid sinus, and right maxillary sinus and expansion of the right frontal sinus and right ethmoid sinus' appears literally in the vignette but describes sinus opacification and expansion without bone destruction; it does not clinically support orbital involvement specifically, as no orbital abnormality is noted in the CT findings.
